learning_outcomes: Identify and describe different energy stores: gravitational PE, kinetic, chemical, thermal, elastic, nuclear, electromagnetic
State the principle of conservation of energy: energy cannot be created or destroyed
Describe energy transfer chains for common situations (falling object, burning fuel, pendulum)
Draw and interpret Sankey diagrams with arrow widths proportional to energy amounts
Recall and use W = Fd to calculate work done, force, or distance
State that work done equals energy transferred and understand the conditions for work to be done
Find work done from the area under a force–distance graph
Recall and use P = W/t = E/t to calculate power, energy, or time
Use P = Fv for an object moving at constant velocity under a constant force (Extended)
Recall and use ΔE_p = mgΔh for gravitational potential energy
Recall and use E_k = ½mv² for kinetic energy
Apply conservation of energy to convert between GPE and KE (with and without energy losses)
Calculate efficiency as useful energy output ÷ total energy input; use as a fraction or percentage
Use efficiency = useful power output ÷ total power input (Extended)
